It was represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] from 1987–2022.{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |title=Roster of Philippine legislators |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=March 3, 2021}} The district covered 25 interior municipalities of eastern Maguindanao bordering the provinces of [[Cotabato]] and [[Sultan Kudarat]], including its capital [[Buluan]].{{cite web|url=https://www.chanrobles.com/ordinance.htm |title=The 1987 Constitution of the Republic of the Philippines |publisher=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library |accessdate=March 3, 2021}} From 2006 to 2008, the district was briefly replaced by the lone district of Maguindanao after a new province was carved out of the [[Maguindanao's 1st congressional district|1st district]] known as [[Shariff Kabunsuan]] which was eventually nullified by the [[Supreme Court of the Philippines|Supreme Court]]. It was last represented in the [[19th Congress of the Philippines|19th Congress]] by Mohamad P. Paglas of the [[Nacionalista Party]] (NP), who was later redistricted to the [[Maguindanao del Sur's at-large congressional district|at-large district]] of the newly-established province of [[Maguindanao del Sur]].{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/members/ |title=House Members |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=March 3, 2021}} ==Representation history== {| class=wikitable |- ! rowspan="2" | # ! rowspan="2" colspan=2 | Image ! rowspan="2" | Member ! colspan=2 | Term of office ! rowspan="2" | Congress ! rowspan="2" | Party ! rowspan="2" | Electoral history ! rowspan="2" | Constituent
